title: Haskell Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: main is the starting action. putStrLn writes a line of text.

examples.title: Name a value
examples.description: A name can stand for a value. Haskell names do not work like boxes that are updated later.

examples.title: Name a calculation
examples.description: Functions take inputs written after their name. This function doubles a number.

examples.title: Write a type guide
examples.description: A type signature describes inputs and results. Int -> Int means a whole number in and out.
examples.code:
twice :: Int -> Int
twice n = n * 2
main = print (twice 4)

examples.title: Choose with if
examples.description: An if expression always has then and else parts because it must produce a value.
examples.code:
message score = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
main = putStrLn (message 8)

examples.title: Read a short list
examples.description: A list keeps values of one type in order. head reads the first item.

examples.title: Change every item
examples.description: map applies a function to each list item and returns a new list.

examples.title: Keep matching items
examples.description: filter keeps items that pass a true-or-false test.

examples.title: Handle list shapes
examples.description: Pattern matching selects steps based on a value shape. [] is an empty list; x:_ has a first item.

examples.title: Repeat with a smaller job
examples.description: A recursive function calls itself. This one stops at zero, then adds numbers on the way back.
examples.code:
sumTo n
  | n <= 0 = 0
  | otherwise = n + sumTo (n - 1)
main = print (sumTo 3)

examples.title: Show that a value may be absent
examples.description: Maybe holds Nothing or Just a value. Pattern matching handles both safely.
examples.code:
showScore Nothing = "No score"
showScore (Just n) = show n
main = putStrLn (showScore (Just 8))

examples.title: Build a list from a rule
examples.description: A list comprehension chooses inputs, filters them and builds new results.
